name: Times for Recitation of Shema
notes: Laws governing the earliest and latest times for reciting Shema in the morning and evening

name: Blessings Accompanying Shema
notes: The blessings recited before and after Shema in both morning and evening: Yotzer Or, Ahavah Rabbah, Emet veYatziv, Emet veEmunah, Hashkivenu

name: Intention in Shema (Kavvanah)
notes: The requirement to have intent while reciting Shema, and whether reading Torah that happened to be Shema fulfills the obligation

name: Interruptions During Shema
notes: Laws concerning permissible and impermissible interruptions between paragraphs of Shema and within each paragraph, including greeting others

name: Posture for Reciting Shema
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether one must recline at night and stand in the morning, or may recite in any position

name: Order of Shema Paragraphs
notes: The rationale for ordering the three paragraphs of Shema as they are, including acceptance of yoke of Heaven before yoke of mitzvot

name: Times for Prayer (Amida)
notes: The latest permissible times for Shacharit, Mincha, Maariv, and Musaf prayers

name: Facing Jerusalem During Prayer
notes: Requirement to face toward the Temple/Holy of Holies when praying; adjustments for those traveling by donkey, ship, etc.

name: Preparation for Prayer (Kavanah and Stillness)
notes: The early pious would wait one hour before praying to achieve proper gravity and submission; not interrupting prayer even for a king or snake

name: Fixed Prayer vs. Supplication
notes: Rabbi Eliezer's ruling that one whose prayer is fixed (mechanical) has not properly supplicated; the ideal of kavvanah in prayer

name: Prayer in Dangerous Situations
notes: Abbreviated prayer for one walking in a dangerous place; Rabbi Yehoshua's formula of short prayer

name: Prayer Leader (Shaliach Tzibbur)
notes: Laws of the communal prayer leader, including replacement when he errs, what constitutes heretical additions to prayer, and birchat kohanim in this context

name: Musaf Prayer
notes: Additional prayer corresponding to the Musaf offering; times and quorum requirements for Musaf

name: Mention of Rain in Amida (Geshem/Tal)
notes: Recitation of 'mashiv haruach' in the second blessing and the request for rain in the ninth blessing of the Amida

name: Havdalah Blessings and Their Order
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel on the order of candle, spices, Grace after Meals, and havdalah blessings; also the exact wording of the candle blessing

name: Havdalah in the Amida
notes: Dispute between Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Eliezer regarding in which blessing of the Amida havdalah is inserted

name: Zimmun (Invitation for Grace After Meals)
notes: Laws of the zimmun — the formal invitation to recite Grace after Meals jointly; who counts toward the quorum, formula for different group sizes, division of groups

name: Place of Recitation for Grace After Meals
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether one who forgot to recite Grace after Meals must return to the place where he ate

name: Grace After Meals for Special Foods
hebrew: ברכת המזון על פירות שבעת המינים
notes: Dispute whether full three-blessing Grace after Meals or abbreviated single blessing is required after eating fruit of the seven species

name: Blessings over Categories of Food
notes: Specific blessings for tree fruits (borei pri haetz), ground produce (borei pri haadama), bread (hamotzi), wine (borei pri hagafen), vegetables, and the catch-all shehakol

name: Priority of Seven Species in Blessings
notes: Which food to bless first when multiple foods are present; dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbis regarding priority of seven species

name: One Blessing Exempting Another
notes: When a blessing over a primary food exempts a secondary food from its own blessing; the principle of ikar and tafel

name: Primary and Secondary Food (Ikar veTafel)
notes: The principle that a blessing over the primary food exempts the secondary food accompanying it from a separate blessing

name: Order of Kiddush Blessings
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether the blessing over wine or over the day comes first in kiddush

name: Handwashing at a Meal (Netilat Yadayim)
notes: Laws of handwashing before and after a meal, including the dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about the order of washing and mixing wine

name: Final Waters (Mayim Acharonim)
notes: Washing hands after a meal before Grace after Meals; dispute about whether to sweep the house first or wash first

name: Immersion for Baal Keri (Ezra's Decree)
notes: Ezra's decree requiring immersion before Torah study and prayer for one who experienced a seminal emission; what Torah activities are permitted beforehand

name: Distancing from Filth for Prayer
notes: Requirement to distance at least four cubits from urine and feces before reciting Shema or praying

name: Groom's Exemption from Shema
notes: A groom is exempt from reciting Shema on his wedding night due to preoccupation; Rabban Gamliel's practice of reciting it anyway

name: Mourner's Exemption from Mitzvot
notes: One whose deceased is before him is exempt from Shema, Amida, and tefillin; pallbearers' exemptions; Rabban Gamliel bathing after his wife's death as one who is delicate

name: Blessings on Natural Phenomena
notes: Blessings over lightning, thunder, storms, mountains, seas, rivers, deserts, the great sea, and shooting stars

name: Blessing on Places of Miracles
notes: Blessing recited upon seeing a place where miracles were performed for Israel; blessing upon seeing where idolatry was eradicated

name: Blessing on Good and Bad Tidings
notes: Reciting 'hatov vehameitiv' for good tidings and 'dayyan ha'emet' for bad tidings; obligation to bless for bad just as for good

name: Traveler's Prayer (Tefillat HaDerech)
notes: Prayer upon entering and exiting a city; Ben Azzai's view of four prayers — two upon entrance and two upon exit

name: Vain Prayer (Tefillat Shav)
notes: Prohibition against praying for something that has already occurred or cannot be changed, e.g., praying the sex of an already-conceived child

name: Respectful Conduct Toward the Temple Mount
notes: Prohibition against entering Temple Mount with staff, shoes, money belt, or dust on feet; not using it as a shortcut; not spitting there; not acting with levity opposite the eastern gate

name: Mentioning God's Name in Greetings
notes: Rabbinic institution to greet others using God's name, as Boaz did; derived from biblical precedent to prevent neglect of this custom

name: Temple Blessing Conclusion Formula
notes: The change in blessing conclusion formula in the Temple from 'until the world' (haolam) to 'from world to world' (min haolam ve'ad haolam) due to Sadducee heresy about the afterlife

name: Women and Minors — Obligations in Mitzvot
notes: Women, slaves, and minors are exempt from Shema and tefillin but obligated in prayer, mezuza, and Grace after Meals; they do not count for zimmun

name: Mentioning Exodus at Night
notes: Obligation to mention the Exodus from Egypt at night as part of Shema; derived by Ben Zoma from 'all the days of your life'; dispute with Rabbis about inclusion of messianic era

name: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel Disputes (Meals/Prayer)
hebrew: מחלוקות בית שמאי ובית הלל בסעודה ותפילה
notes: The series of disputes between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding kiddush, handwashing, havdalah, and meal practices in tractate Berakhot

name: Prayer upon Entering/Exiting Study Hall
notes: Rabbi Nechunia ben HaKana's practice of reciting a brief prayer upon entering and exiting the beit midrash for protection from mishaps and gratitude

name: Abbreviated Amida (Tefillah Ketzarah)
notes: Dispute among Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Yehoshua, and Rabbi Akiva about whether the full eighteen blessings or an abbreviated form is required

name: Fluency of Prayer as Omen of Acceptance
notes: Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa's practice of knowing whether his prayer for the sick was accepted based on whether it was fluent in his mouth; erring in prayer as bad omen

name: Blessing over Diluted vs. Undiluted Wine
hebrew: ברכה על יין מזוג ושאינו מזוג
notes: Dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbis whether a blessing may be recited over undiluted wine or only after water is added

name: Blessing over Incense at a Meal
notes: One who blesses over wine at the end of a meal also recites the blessing over the incense (mugmar) brought after the meal

name: Blessing over Fire/Candle at Havdalah
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai (bara, past tense) and Beit Hillel (boreh, present tense) for the candle blessing; prohibition against blessing over gentile fire, fire for the dead, or fire of idolatry

name: Responding Amen to Another's Blessing
notes: One answers amen after a Jew even if he did not hear the full blessing; but one does not answer amen after a Samaritan unless he heard the full blessing
